title: System Design Interview - An insiders guide volume 3

blocks.text: A notification system is a set of services that sends messages to users. These messages can be alerts, updates, or reminders. The system uses APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) to allow different services to send notifications.
The system has different parts, referred to as Service 1 to N. Each of these parts sends notifications using APIs provided by notification servers.
Notification servers are crucial components of the system. They have specific tasks that help manage notifications. Here are their main functions:
They provide APIs for services to send notifications. These APIs are available only within the system or to verified users. This restriction helps stop spam.
They perform basic checks to confirm that email addresses and phone numbers are valid.
They access the database or cache to find the necessary data that completes a notification.
They send notification information to message queues. This allows multiple notifications to be processed at the same time.

script:
Notification servers are key parts of a notification system. They take care of sending messages to users. They do this by using APIs, which are tools that allow services to communicate. Each server makes sure the messages are sent out correctly. This is crucial for keeping everything running smoothly.

Now, let’s look at what these servers do. They provide APIs that let other services send messages. These APIs are restricted to avoid spam. They check email addresses and phone numbers to ensure they’re valid. They also pull necessary info from databases or caches. Finally, they take the notification details and send them to message queues. This lets multiple messages go out at once, so everything runs efficiently. What does that mean for the user? It means they get their notifications quickly and without hassle.
